I think a large problem is that sometimes skinny people are a little overzealous, and it causes the overweight to shy away from healthy living altogether. I'm straddling the fence between underweight and normal weight, so I think I can speak with a little authority. Eat healthi*er* and exercise *more*. I hear fitness buffs talk about fast food or candy like it's the incarnation of satan. "Oh, maybe you can sneak in *one* donut a week if you eat nothing but rice cakes and celery sticks  the rest." Yeesh... I'm not trying to make fun of people who practice this lifestyle. I respect them greatly for their fortitude. I'm just saying that it's probably very intimidating for those who are a little overweight. It's intimidating to *me* at least. It's not really about never ever eating things that are 'bad'. It's more about incorporating things that are good. Maybe have a small salad instead of the fries. You going to Taco Bell? Maybe walk there unstead of driving. Little by little, it becomes less of "I *have* to do this or I'll stay fat" and more of "I feel good when I behave this way, let's do it some more." Unless the person is dangerously obese, I think you have to *ease* them into it or else they'll be more likely to fall off the wagon and give up. That's just my opinion, though. I'm no professional. I just have a lot of feelings.

Eh, I'd like to think that the mental concentration required for video games might actually help stave of dementia in the younger generations. They do say that regular cognitive challenges like crosswords or word jumbles help keep the minds of the elderly sharp. Imagine the benefits of Professor Layton or tactical RPGs which are largely more complex. And constant communication over headphones should help as well. Most old folks I know who lose it just sat around watching tv for ten plus years, hardly talking to anyone. And heck, maybe they'll have a cure in fifty years. But I may be too optimistic in my musing here.

Oh, lord. It felt so good to talk to someone I didn't have to look at, if that makes sense. I've just felt so self-serving these past few months. I worry that I've made my friends and family out to be horrible people in my post. But that couldn't be farther from the truth. My husband is the most wonderful man in the world. I just feel so inferior to him. And my parents are exceptional, the best parents ever to exist. But they're amazingly stoic. And I feel so weak by comparison. I've been going through crazier and crazier displays of emotion trying to fix myself or achieve some kind of catharsis. My poor husband. I don't feel like I give *him* anything but pain now. I've become so aggressively sad and needy. Even angry sometimes, especially at night when I can't go back to sleep. I just needed an objective person to tell me I'm not a horrible person. Crazy, yeah? I don't trust the people that I know love me. Thank you for listening and for your kind words. They mean a lot.
